summary: Static Astro site on Cloudflare (Workers static assets / Pages) (global CDN) with no backend or database. Estimated $0/month (within the $0 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: Pre-rendered pages served from a CDN with no server tier: nothing to patch or scale for a read-only site.

frontend.justification: Web - Astro: Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; static-first output for a content_site (scale.workload=read_heavy); server-rendered/pre-rendered HTML for seo_critical=true.

alternatives.why_not: Astro scores higher on maintainability (fit 12.9 vs 13.3).
Astro scores higher on learning curve and maintainability (fit 12.3 vs 13.3).

tradeoffs: App-like interactivity needs islands/hydration per component
Smaller ecosystem than React meta-frameworks for complex apps

backend.justification: No dynamic requirement: project.type=content_site, auth=none, payments/realtime/uploads/ML all false, workload=read_heavy. Pages are generated at build time, so there is no server to run.

alternatives.why_not: nothing to execute per request; would add cost and attack surface for no benefit

tradeoffs: Add a server tier later only if dynamic features (forms, auth, comments) appear

database.justification: No persistent application data: content is authored as files in the repository and compiled at build time (Markdown, per project.description)

alternatives.why_not: adds a moving part and cost for content a single author edits as files

tradeoffs: Add a server tier later only if dynamic features (forms, auth, comments) appear

hosting.justification: Chosen because serves pre-built static files from a global CDN; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3; free tier fits budget.monthly_infra_usd=0.

alternatives.why_not: Cloudflare scores higher on cost and performance (fit 9.6 vs 9.6).
Cloudflare scores higher on cost and performance (fit 9.6 vs 9.6).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud is not on-premise.

tradeoffs: Cloudflare now steers new projects from Pages to Workers static assets

supporting.justification: Chosen because the hosting platform already serves through a global CDN; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=4; free tier fits budget.monthly_infra_usd=0.

alternatives.why_not: Built-in CDN of Cloudflare scores higher on integration with the hosting platform (fit 8.3 vs 8.7).
Built-in CDN of Cloudflare scores higher on integration with the hosting platform and time-to-market (fit 4.5 vs 8.7).

supporting.justification: Chosen because Git push deploys with previews are built into the hosting; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=4; free tier fits budget.monthly_infra_usd=0.

alternatives.why_not: Git-push deploys on Cloudflare scores higher on integration with the hosting platform (fit 5.5 vs 6.8).
Git-push deploys on Cloudflare scores higher on integration with the hosting platform and cost (fit 3.6 vs 6.8).

supporting.justification: Chosen because static site: platform analytics are enough; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=4; free tier fits budget.monthly_infra_usd=0.

alternatives.why_not: Cloudflare analytics/logs scores higher on fit for the project type and cost (fit 4.5 vs 6.2).
Needs ongoing operations work but team.has_devops=false (ops burden 3/5). Cloudflare analytics/logs scores higher on fit for the project type and time-to-market (fit 0.5 vs 6.2).

assumptions: Order-of-magnitude band from approximate public list prices (USD) in the knowledge base; not a quote
Sized for 3,000 users at 12 months, 50 peak concurrent users, ~5 req/s peak (scale tier: tiny)
Data: ~1 GB in the database, ~0 GB of media, ~15 GB/month egress
Excludes taxes, developer salaries, domain names, app-store fees and one-off migration work

breakdown.basis: tiny tier (~5 req/s peak, 50 concurrent users)

warnings.message: Runs entirely on free tiers; traffic spikes beyond fair-use limits may need a paid plan.
